London, 26<sup>th</sup> February 2009 



# **Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest** 

**Ridge Mining plc** announced that its 50% owned subsidiary, Blue Ridge Platinum Limited, has closed out all its hedging arrangements generating a surplus of Rand 541m (US$54 million). This will be used to reduce the project’s borrowings and to provide additional working capital for the mine during the ramp-up phase. 

_Source:  Ridge Mining_ 

**Volkswagen AG** , the biggest overseas carmaker in China, plans to add at least four new models a year in the country until 2018 as it strives to double local sales.  The vehicles will include Audi, Volkswagen and Skoda brand cars.  Volkswagen sold 1.02 million vehicles in China last year as demand for models such as the Santana helped it outpace the wider auto market, Asia’s biggest. The company intends to boost sales further by winning more customers in smaller cities and by doubling its number of dealers. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Auto-parts maker Visteon Corp** . warned today it might breach its debt covenants following a steep quarterly loss and said it was considering disposing of substantial assets to address liquidity needs. Visteon, the former parts affiliate of Ford Motor Co., said the continued downturn in the global auto industry and tight credit markets have put a squeeze on its financial results, cash flows and liquidity. Shares of Visteon fell 13 percent to 13 cents. The stock has lost 96 percent of its value in the past year. Laurie Harbour-Felax, an automotive industry consultant, said it was likely that the company would file for bankruptcy “soon.” _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Platinum Guild International** (PGI) announced that retail sales for the first three days of 2009 in China rose 13% year-on-year, showing that the government’s efforts to spur domestic demand and prevent an economic slowdown are yielding results.  PGI predicts that coming growth will be caused by a combination of several factors in China, namely a drop in platinum prices as a result of falling industrial demand, proactive domestic fiscal policies stimulating domestic spending, Chinese consumers’ love for platinum, and the ongoing promotion of platinum over the past decade.  According to the Shanghai Gold Exchange, platinum purchases increased by 16% year-on-year in 2008.  According to a survey conducted by PGI, 17 key retailers in northern China reported a significant increase in platinum jewelry sales over Christmas and the New Year. In southern China, platinum sales grew by 20-30% over Christmas and by 15-50% over the New Year season, with Shanghai reporting the greatest growth. According to the latest figures released by PGI, retail sales for the first three days of 2009 rose 13% year-on-year. _Source:  China Daily_ 

**Platinum** rose for the first time in three days yesterday on demand for an alternative investment as U.S. stocks tumbled amid pessimism over the global economic outlook. Palladium dropped. The Standard & Poor’s

500 Index fell for the seventh time in eight sessions on concern that the credit crisis is deepening. The metal has climbed 12 percent this year, while the S&P 500 is down 15 percent. Platinum futures for April delivery climbed $10.40, or 1 percent, to $1,059.10 an ounce on the New York Mercantile Exchange. The price dropped 4.3 percent in the previous two days. “Platinum is largely a play on the very sick global car market,” John Reade, the head metals strategist for UBS AG in London, said. “We are concerned that investors are buying platinum for the wrong reasons and believe the argument that platinum never trades at a prolonged or deep discount to gold could be tested this year.” _Source:  Bloomberg_
